lines: One chunk holds at least 90.0 % of a page, so the browser fetches practically the whole page before it shows anything:
procest-main.js: 1 file, 4,086,322 B, and 1 chunk of 175,463 B its runtime loads later, of which procest-main.js is 4,086,322 B (95.9 %).
procest-settings.js: 1 file, 3,683,299 B, and 1 chunk of 175,463 B its runtime loads later, of which procest-settings.js is 3,683,299 B (95.5 %).

Code splitting puts what the first paint does not need behind a dynamic import, and then the browser fetches it when the code asks. Which part of a page that is does not follow from the build output; the source decides it.
2 packages are imported by their root in src, so the whole barrel is reachable and the bundler keeps whatever it cannot prove unused:

@nextcloud/vue: 1,583,126 B in 242 modules, 38.7 % of the static path of procest-main.js, imported by its root in 23 files: App.vue (NcAppContent, NcContent, NcLoadingIcon), navigation/MainMenu.vue (NcAppNavigation, NcAppNavigationItem, NcAppNavigationSettings), and 21 more.

@conduction/nextcloud-vue: 176,861 B in 14 modules, 4.3 % of the static path of procest-main.js, imported by its root in 7 files: App.vue (CnIndexSidebar), store/modules/object.js (auditTrailsPlugin, createObjectStore, filesPlugin, ...), and 5 more. It is imported per module as well, through 1 other specifier.
Importing the module that is used instead of the package root lets the bundler drop the rest of the barrel.
ncmake's lint-vue-imports workflow gates exactly this specifier for @nextcloud/vue, so this finding is that red check with a byte figure attached.
Built with: webpack.config.js, package.json declares @nextcloud/webpack-vue-config ^6.0.1, webpack ^5.94.0.
